# Code generated by otio-sdk-gen from crates/otio-capi. DO NOT EDIT.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(opentimelineio-cpp LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

# The headers are header-only; the work is in libotio, which they call.
add_library(opentimelineio INTERFACE)
add_library(opentimelineio::opentimelineio ALIAS opentimelineio)

# The variables above set the standard for what this directory compiles, and
# this library compiles nothing: the headers are compiled by whoever includes
# them. So the requirement travels with the target, or a consumer added with
# add_subdirectory builds `std::optional` in its own older language mode.
target_compile_features(opentimelineio INTERFACE cxx_std_17)

# The C interface's own header, read where it lives rather than copied, so
# the package cannot describe an older interface than the library.
target_include_directories(opentimelineio INTERFACE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../crates/otio-capi/include")

target_link_directories(opentimelineio INTERFACE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib")
target_link_libraries(opentimelineio INTERFACE otio)

if(APPLE)
    target_link_libraries(opentimelineio INTERFACE
        "-framework CoreFoundation" "-framework Security" iconv)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_link_libraries(opentimelineio INTERFACE pthread dl m)
endif()

include(CTest)
if(BUILD_TESTING)
    add_executable(otio-tests tests/tests.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(otio-tests PRIVATE opentimelineio)
    # The tests read the same fixtures the Rust tests do, so they need to know
    # where the repository is rather than guess it from __FILE__.
    target_compile_definitions(otio-tests PRIVATE
        OTIO_REPOSITORY="${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../..")
    add_test(NAME otio-tests COMMAND otio-tests)
endif()
